pr_comments:
I added a `StataNonCatValueLabel` to format value labels for non categorical variables. In the `StataWriter`:
* added `value_labels` as optional argument. The format is as close to what is returned from `StataReader.value_labels()`, but the keys should be column names instead of column labels
* renamed `_is_col_cat` to `_has_value_labels`
* `_prepare_non_cat_value_labels` formats the value labels and checks that columns exist and are numeric
Thanks for the feedback! I made the typing changes and will go ahead and create a sample dta for some additional tests

You need to import Literal when type checking, and make sure `from __future__ import annotations` is at the top of the file.

An example:

https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/accf345fdd4fb92056a5e62d4105fc8f4491ff2c/pandas/core/series.py#L141-L144

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16855568/116783231-9c8a7e80-aa5b-11eb-8028-14f7723983de.png)

I also moved the creation of `_converted_names` above `_prepare_pandas`, it was being populated in prepare pandas and reset to an empty dict in init

issue_context.title: ENH: option to export df to Stata dataset with value labels
issue_context.body:
#### Is your feature request related to a problem?

One feature of Stata (.dta) datasets is that it's possible to have categorical columns with numerical values and string value labels. At the moment, `df.to_stata` doesn't have an option to create this kind of columns.

#### Describe the solution you'd like

It would be nice if `df.to_stata` could have a `value_labels` option that accepts a dictionary mapping numerical values to value labels. 

#### API breaking implications

.
#### Describe alternatives you've considered

.
#### Additional context

.
comments:
Can you check that this isn't already happening/supported? Note that the pandas has its own implementation of this feature. Pandas' implementation of numerically-encoded string values is a Categorical dtype with string categories. Thus to the extent pandas would support this it wouldn't be by having a `value_labels` kwarg in the `to_stata` method, but rather by calling `to_stata` on a Categorical-typed object.

I don't have access to Stata to see what this looks like there, but I can verify that if I write out a Categorical Series as Stata format, it is read back as Categorical when using pandas read_stata, so it seems that pandas must be encoding the categories and codes in the Stata file somehow.

```
In [15]: df = pd.DataFrame({'a':['a', 'b', 'a']})

In [16]: df['a'] = df['a'].astype('category')

In [17]: df.to_stata('C:/temp/df.dta', write_index=False)

In [18]: df2 = pd.read_stata('C:/temp/df.dta')

In [19]: df2
Out[19]:
   a
0  a
1  b
2  a

In [20]: df2.dtypes
Out[20]:
a    category
```

Can you verify that using the above code appears in Stata as a categorical variable?

Thank you for looking into this.

I can confirm that df['a'] is indeed read in Stata as a numerical variable with value labels, with 0:'a', 1:'b'. 

I think this gets Stata users most of the way in almost all cases. One remaining problem would be control over the numeric values. In Stata, it is possible to have something like 1:'a', 3:'b'. It appears that the values that the `to_stata` method exports are always ordered from 0 to max, incremented by 1, based on the ordering.

One can change the order of the underlying values by using `Categorical.reorder_categories()` or `Categorical.set_categories()`. But there is no control of the values, is that right?

This is probably not big enough of a problem to implement a new feature though.

General support could be added to non-categoricals in `StataWriter`, `StataWriter117` and `StataWriterUTF8`. The natural syntax would probably be a dictionary of dictionaries where the keys in the other dictionary are column names and the inner dictionary contains the value labels.

I wasn't sure how to best deal with the duplication, the only difference between the existing StataValueLabel and new non-categorical value label is the init: the non-categorical takes the label name and a dict of value labels directly, the existing `StataValueLabel` is created from a categorical series and pulls the name and labels from it.

The two options I've thought of for getting rid of the duplication are:
* change `StataValueLabel` to init from a label name and value_labels dictionary then add a `from_cat` method to extract the name and label from a Categorical
* add labname and value_labels to the StataValueLabel init and let it be created from either those or the catarray

Both would get rid of the new non categorical label class entirely, the first would be a breaking change to StataValueLabel. Would one of these be acceptable or is there a better way that I'm not thinking of?
@jreback I moved the duplicated attribute definitions to _prepare_value_labels. Would either of the changes from above be better?
why don't you rename this to _cat_value_labels to distingish and make consistent

_value_labels is a combined list of categorical and non-categorical labels. there isn't a standalone _cat_value_labels because they're added straight to _value_labels after converting categoricals in the dataframe
